clue.text: Kept on and on and pluckily played?

definitions.meaning: to keep on and on about something is to dwell on it tiresomely
a harpist plucks the strings, so pluckily played is a playful way of describing harp music

explanation.definitionFit: To keep returning tediously to a topic is idiomatically to harp on it; the instrument is also played by plucking.

clue.text: Charge supporter overcome by drink

indicators.note: overcome by means the supporter is engulfed within the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
a leg supports a table or body

explanation.surface: A fan who has had too much to drink is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to accuse or claim, to charge someone with something.

clue.text: Locate a job

definitions.meaning: a post or situation in employment

explanation.definitionFit: Position is a verb meaning place and a noun meaning a post of employment.

clue.text: Departs on frigate damaged by floating material

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: damaged signals the warship's letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A warship leaves port, damaged by debris in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftage is matter carried along by the current, drifting debris.

clue.text: Current producers requiring extremely reliable cast

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the cast of a play is its actors

explanation.surface: A nuclear plant manager wants a cast-iron reliable workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an adverb strengthening 'reliable', but it takes that word's first and last letters, R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear reactors generate electricity, so they produce electric current.

clue.text: Deplores birds getting run over

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the letter above the rest

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
egrets are white herons

explanation.surface: Someone is upset when birds are struck by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to be sorry about it, so regrets means deplores.

clue.text: Performed church music as girl conducted

parts.note: Carol is a girl's name
led means guided or conducted

explanation.surface: A girl leads the choir in singing hymns.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing carols, festive songs of the church.

clue.text: Working with special hunter to find fugitive

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: special suggests the letters are given a special new order

explanation.surface: An elite tracker is engaged to locate an escaped convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fleeing capture is said idiomatically to be running from the law.

clue.text: Examiner can always see Southern vineyard first

indicators.note: first puts the south and the vineyard ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a cru is a French wine-growing estate
a tin is a can
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: An inspector can always visit a southern wine estate first.
explanation.walkthrough: CRU is French for a classified vineyard or its wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer examines things closely, especially election ballots.

clue.text: Many getting a beating, coming to blows

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken in crosswords as many
a lashing is a beating with a whip

explanation.surface: A crowd gets a thrashing in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashing means fighting or colliding, which is what people coming to blows do.

clue.text: Fixed price accepted by creditor in depression

indicators.note: accepted by means the price is taken inside the creditor's abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for creditor
a rate is a fixed price or charge

explanation.surface: A creditor's set price leaves a debtor feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' tempts as low spirits after money trouble; here it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow, a depression in the earth's surface.

clue.text: First noble that is a paragon of virtue, too

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
ST abbreviates saint, a paragon of virtue

explanation.surface: A nobleman who was the first of his line was also a model of goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means first in time.

clue.text: Fellow worker accepting sit-in is liable to lose?

indicators.note: accepting means the pair of words take another word inside them

parts.note: HE, a male, stands for a fellow
an ant is the classic worker insect
sit is taken as written from the clue's sit-in

explanation.surface: A colleague joining a sit-in protest seems likely to lose out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit-in' reads as a protest, but only its first word is used and 'in' is a link word; 'accepting' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hesitant player wavers and so is likely to be beaten, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hold not full, as result of drink with leading seaman

parts.note: a half is a half pint of beer
Admiral Nelson is Britain's most famous sailor

explanation.surface: A drinker grapples with a sailor after a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: A half nelson is a wrestling hold, a lesser form of the full nelson, so the definition hints at both.
explanation.definitionFit: This wrestling grip is the partial version of the full nelson.

clue.text: Famous swimmer's name featured in editorial

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: featured in means the abbreviation is placed inside the next word

parts.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial

explanation.surface: A celebrated swimmer gets a mention in the newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth who swam the Hellespont to meet Hero is a legendary swimmer.

clue.text: Sailor's leaflet is appropriate

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; with the 's it gives ABS
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: A sailor's pamphlet is suitable reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb: to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to remove or take away, a formal verb for steal.

clue.text: Quick to rise, coming in to meal that's diabolical

indicators.note: coming in to means the reversed word goes inside the meal

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal

indicators.note: in a down answer, to rise means read the word upwards

parts.note: quick in its old sense means alive, live

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to dinner with fiendish intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns LIVE upwards into EVIL. Quick means living, as in the quick and the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish means fiendish, like the devil.

clue.text: Lively dance to church rhythm

indicators.note: lively suggests the letters jump around into a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Energetic dancing to church music has a strong beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is a rhythmic flow or beat in sound or speech.

clue.text: Dignitary planting tree on island

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: the alder is a tree
the Isle of Man is in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A civic leader plants a tree on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior civic official, a local dignitary.

clue.text: Slow mover races badly, caught at the end

indicators.note: at the end places the catching word after the rest
badly signals the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: got means caught

explanation.surface: A slowcoach runs poor races and is overtaken at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: An escargot is a snail, proverbially slow-moving.

clue.text: Coming from the centre, restricting Conservative. extremist

indicators.note: restricting means the first phrase hems in the abbreviation

parts.note: radial means spreading out from a central point

explanation.surface: A Tory moving out from the centre ground becomes extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints a stray full stop after 'Conservative'; it plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical holds extreme views, seeking root-and-branch change.

clue.text: Unusually bad court in Paris, for example

indicators.note: unusually signals the following words are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A trial in the French capital was strangely bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the city, but is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris abducted Helen of Troy, making him a kidnapper.

clue.text: Resist work and strike an attitude

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to pose is to adopt a posture

explanation.surface: A worker refuses to toil and takes a stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to fight against or resist it.

clue.text: Required dateline to be edited

indicators.note: editing a text rearranges it, so the word before is to be reordered

explanation.surface: A newspaper story needed its dateline revised.
explanation.definitionFit: If something entails a consequence it requires it, so entailed means required.

clue.text: Not circulating — that spoils the reception

definitions.meaning: electrical interference crackling on a radio ruins the signal

explanation.definitionFit: Static is both an adjective for motionless and a noun for crackling interference on broadcasts.

clue.text: Relief work involving energy by hundreds eventually succeeded

indicators.note: involving means the relief carving takes the energy inside itself

parts.note: a cameo is a carving in relief
go means energy or vigour
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so it stands for hundreds

explanation.surface: Aid efforts powered by hundreds of volunteers finally paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' suggests aid work but is a raised carving. 'by' just sets D beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To come good is an idiom for turning out well after a poor start.

clue.text: Hazel's protector is briefly in it

definitions.meaning: the hard shell guards the hazelnut inside
to put something in a ... is to say it concisely

explanation.surface: Someone called Hazel's guardian sums things up in a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut's casing protects it, and the idiom in a nutshell means put concisely.

clue.text: New number that's lower

parts.note: ether numbs, so it is a number, a thing that makes numb

explanation.surface: A new figure comes in lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as something that numbs: the anaesthetic ether.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old word for lower, as in the nether regions.
